en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kiṅkaṇikapupphiya Chapter on the Tamālapupphiya Group, Number Nine The Apadāna of the Elder Kiṅkaṇikapupphiya: When I was a merchant in the city of Benares, I saw the Buddha, the Blessed One, the Teacher, Seated upon a seat in the midst of the assembly. Having seen him, I took a kiṅkaṇika flower And offered it with a devout heart to the Buddha. Because of that root of merit, I have been reborn In a wealthy family, possessing great riches. For eighty-four thousand years, I lived as a householder, Enjoying the pleasures of the five senses. Then, having renounced the world, I went forth into homelessness; I am now an arahant, free from all taints. By this truth, may the world be well. Thus did the Elder Kiṅkaṇikapupphiya speak.
“Named Sumaṅgala,
the Self-Existent Aparājita,
having emerged from the forest, ...
The Victor entered the city.
Having wandered for alms and departed from the city, the Sage—
The Fully Awakened One, having accomplished his task,
dwells at will within the forest;
having plucked a kiṅkaṇī flower—
With a clear heart and joyful mind, I offered it to the Buddha,
the Self-Existent One, the Great Sage.
In ninety-four eons ago,
because I offered that flower,
I have not known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
In the eighty-sixth aeon from now,
one named Apilāsi;
Endowed with the seven treasures,
a wheel-turning monarch of great power;
the four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Elder Thera Kiṅkaṇikapupphiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Kiṅkaṇikapupphiya is the ninth.
